_note: v6: v5 + CNN ensemble. Score-level ensemble of v5 and aniq_baseline_independent_cnn: both members' scores are converted to log-probabilities over the 333 pairs and mixed as w * v5 + (1 - w) * CNN; w and gamma are chosen on the validation split. Motivation: equal seen accuracy (uncalibrated 67.1% vs 67.2%) from very different models (CLIP prompts + LoRA vs fine-tuned ResNet-50s), so their errors should partly differ. No new model is trained: each member is only retrained on the validation split to produce validation scores (cached), and the test scores are the members' saved ones. Ablation of ONE change against v5 (everything else identical, same validation split: seed 42, 1 split). Keep the change only if validation HM beats v5's 51.2% by more than 2 points (v6 measured run-to-run noise of about 3 points: v5 retrained on the same split scored 48.3% vs 51.2%); the test result is recorded but must not decide.
_result: Best result so far. Validation chose weight 0.4 on v5 and 0.6 on aniq_baseline_independent_cnn, gamma 6.6 (log-prob units): test harmonic mean 70.1% top-1 / 93.3% top-5 (v5 alone 65.1% / 92.1%, CNN alone 59.7% / 87.7%). Seen top-1 59.8% (v5 53.4%), unseen top-1 84.8% (v5 83.2%); uncalibrated seen top-1 71.3% (each member about 67%), so the models' errors partly differ and the mix fixes some of each. Validation HM 53.1% vs 48.3% for v5 alone and 44.4% for the CNN alone on the same retrained split (+4.7 points over v5): a clear improvement. Noise finding: v5 retrained here on the same split, seed and settings scored 48.3% validation HM vs 51.2% in the original v5 run, so run-to-run noise is about 3 points, not the assumed 1; single-run differences of a few points between variants are not reliable.
title: cnn_ensemble

ensemble._note: Weight on the first member (v5) from 0 to 1 in steps of 0.1; w = 1 is v5 alone, w = 0 the CNN alone, so validation also reports each member on its own.

validation._note: Same split procedure, seed and settings as v5. gamma is in log-probability units here (both members are on the log-prob scale), so the grid is 0-15 in steps of 0.1; v5's 0.0725 cosine corresponds to 7.25.
